items.claim: The row's rear seam is warranted only by a fronted-subject clause that matches no catalogued frame device, so the cut separating the report from the reward section is under-argued in a stretch the strategy flags for caution over its speaker changes.
items.evidence: וַיהוָ֞ה חָפֵ֤ץ דַּכְּאוֹ֙ (Isa.53.10, byte tier) is a waw-plus-fronted-subject construction naming the divine subject, not an instance of any of the book's catalogued speech-frame formulas (no amar/vayomer root, no koh-amar, no postpositive neum) and not an addressee shift or vocative; the third-person description of the servant's fate continues on both sides of the seam (compare the burial notice at Isa.53.9), and the first unambiguous first-person divine verb is לָכֵ֞ן אֲחַלֶּק (Isa.53.12), two verses later. Cutting at the fronted-subject clause rather than reading the whole confession-and-resolution complex as one continuous unit is a theme-split lacking a tier-1 marker at the cut point itself, precisely where the strategy calls for extra caution over sub-dividing the speaker changes in this stretch.

items.claim: The row's front seam is the same under-argued fronted-subject clause; the strongest rival the row itself discloses already concedes that no explicit change-of-speaker marker precedes the true first-person divine verb two verses later.
items.evidence: The opening clause וַיהוָ֞ה חָפֵ֤ץ דַּכְּאוֹ֙ (Isa.53.10, byte tier) fronts the divine subject but is not a catalogued speech-frame formula, addressee shift, or vocative; the servant continues to be described in the third person through the following verse, and the row's own first-person divine verb, לָכֵ֞ן אֲחַלֶּק (Isa.53.12, byte tier), arrives two verses after the claimed seam. The row's own disclosed rival -- extending the report forward because no explicit speaker change precedes the first-person verb -- is the stronger reading; the closing seam into the fresh vocative address that follows this row is solid, but the opening seam rests on an uncatalogued syntactic signal rather than a tier-1 frame marker.

items.claim: The chapter-span row is bounded by two solid tier-1 signals -- a vocative imperative onset opening it and a correctly role-classified invitation cry closing it -- and rightly declines to fragment at the four intervening divine-speech signatures, none of which carries an accompanying addressee shift.
items.evidence: The vocative-imperative onset opening the chapter and the distinct invitation-class hoy opening the next unit are both explicit, bytes-visible tier-1 markers; the postpositive 'says/declares Yahweh' signatures recurring inside the chapter are correctly held as internal refrain rather than seam triggers, since none is accompanied by a fresh addressee or scene change, consistent with how the book's frame-plus-speech default treats sustained address elsewhere. The disclosed ketiv/qere pair is byte-accurate against the source text, and confidence is capped at the medium_low ceiling appropriate to a whole-chapter span.

items.evidence: The opening hoy is role-classified as an invitation cry rather than blended with the woe-series or self-exclamation uses of the same lexeme elsewhere in the book, matching the book's own role-split for that device; the rear seam at the following imperative onset is a listed tier-1 device class. The qadosh-Israel title's recurrence just past the row's rear seam is disclosed as cross-seam corroboration rather than left silent, consistent with the cross-seam-cohesion discipline.

items.evidence: The imperative onset opening this row at Isa.55.6 is the same listed tier-1 device class that closes the invitation unit at Isa.55.1-Isa.55.5, giving the shared seam a consistent warrant on both sides. The row explicitly weighs and rejects reading the closing nature-personification verses as an isolable doxology, on the correct ground that no fresh imperative or addressee marker opens that stretch -- matching the closed vocabulary's requirement that a doxology be isolable by its own tier-1 signal rather than by texture alone. The rear seam is the ratified parent-frame boundary and is correctly treated as non-negotiable; the disclosed ketiv/qere pair is byte-accurate against the source text.

Every span-relevant parashah mark and the single paseq inside the span are disclosed completely and without conflating mark types.

items.claim: unit_type is declared for the whole row without the mandated one-sentence device_notes disclosure covering the closing verses' shift into lament register.
items.evidence: “The righteous perish, and no one lays it to heart. Merciful men are taken away, and no one considers that the righteous is taken away from the evil.” and “He enters into peace. They rest in their beds, each one who walks in his uprightness.” (web:Isa.57.1-Isa.57.2) read as lament/reflection register, distinct from the satirical indictment of the blind-watchmen material that precedes them; the row's own rationale names this a register shift from satire to lament, yet no sentence in device_notes discloses the operative-category deviation this represents for a row typed as a single judgment_oracle unit. The merge decision itself -- keeping the reflection with the indictment rather than cutting at the chapter division, since no vocative or frame marker intervenes -- is well warranted and is not in question here.
